title: The Small Bakery
premise: Pastry chef Jonah Galloway is three missed payments from losing her café when she learns her late grandmother's stubborn orchard has been deeded jointly to her and Theo Marsh, the boy who once broke her heart and now represents the development firm circling the property. As they're forced to co-manage the orchard to satisfy the deed's inheritance clause, Jonah discovers Theo isn't the corporate shark she assumed — he's sabotaging his own firm from inside to protect the land. When his betrayal of the company surfaces, both their livelihoods hang on one harvest-season deadline, and Jonah must choose between selling out for the money that would save her café or trusting the man who finally sees her clearly. She chooses truth over security, they save the orchard together, and the café survives on a new foundation built with him.
about_author: Edmund Sandoval is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, orchards, and other places where patience is a form of devotion. He lives in rural Oregon with his partner and an ancient sourdough starter named after his grandmother.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Opening in her failing café, we see her discipline everything — recipes, staff, her own heart — as the bank letter arrives. Emotional beat: controlled desperation; she treats love like a muscle she's trained into submission.

chapters.title: The Deed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A lawyer's letter reveals her grandmother left her half of the Hollow Creek orchard — and the other half to Theo Marsh, the name she hasn't spoken in twelve years. Emotional beat: shock curdling into dread as she realizes what sharing means.

chapters.title: The Man at the Gate
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He arrives at the orchard first, ostensibly surveying it for Meridian Development, privately grieving the grandmother who once fed him pie. Emotional beat: guilt wearing a professional mask.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. First confrontation: Theo proposes buying her out; Jonah refuses, citing the deed's clause requiring joint stewardship through one full harvest. Emotional beat: old wounds weaponized into negotiation leverage.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Searching the farmhouse, he finds letters suggesting Grandma Galloway paired them deliberately, believing the orchard could mend what pride broke. Emotional beat: unease that the dead are matchmaking.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Forced to work the trees together, they fall into an old rhythm — banter, competence, accidental closeness. Jonah notices Theo flinching whenever his phone rings. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Meridian's Offer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His boss demands the orchard appraisal by season's end; Theo stalls, lying about soil reports. Meanwhile Jonah's café landlord issues a final notice. Emotional beat: two clocks ticking toward collision.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The café's oven dies; Theo shows up unasked with tools and stays past midnight fixing it. She catches herself laughing and hates how easy it feels. Emotional beat: the trained muscle of her heart twitching against its leash.

chapters.title: The Rival Bidder
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A rival developer, Voss, makes a cash offer directly to Jonah — enough to erase every debt. Theo realizes if she takes it, the deed clause dissolves and so does his excuse to stay. Emotional beat: jealousy revealing feelings he can't manage.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. After a storm strands them in the farmhouse, a near-kiss breaks off when Theo's phone lights up with 'MERIDIAN — URGENT.' He lies about the caller. Emotional beat: intimacy interrupted by the secret widening between them.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Going through Grandma's accounts, Jonah finds payments from Meridian dated years ago — proof the firm has wanted this land for a long time, and that someone inside fed them information. Suspicion lands squarely on Theo. Emotional beat: trust cracking under evidence.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Jonah confronts him; he admits working for Meridian but hides that he's been falsifying reports to kill the deal. Half-truths pile up. Emotional beat: loyalty to his own conscience versus honesty with her.

chapters.title: Voss Moves First
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Voss, tipped off by a mole, offers to buy out Theo's share instead, promising Jonah full ownership and café salvation. Temptation becomes concrete: a signed offer on her counter. Emotional beat: the choice sharpening into a blade.

chapters.title: The Falsified Report
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Meridian discovers his doctored soil assessments; he's suspended pending termination and possible legal action. He drives to the orchard to confess everything and finds Jonah holding Voss's contract. Emotional beat: ruin arriving before courage does.

chapters.title: Everything He Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Theo confesses all — the sabotage, the suspension, the years of regret since he walked away. Jonah, burned by the ledger and the lies of omission, tells him to leave. Emotional beat: heartbreak disguised as prudence.

chapters.title: Signature Line
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV alone at night with Voss's contract and a pen. Flashbacks braid together: Grandma's letters, Theo fixing the oven, the storm. Emotional beat: the darkest hour — she can save everything she built by signing away the person who sees her.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She finds Grandma's final unsent letter to Theo, revealing he'd secretly paid the orchard's back taxes for years and begged her never to tell Jonah. Emotional beat: the ledger reinterpreted — loyalty, not betrayal.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the county zoning hearing deciding the orchard's fate, Theo testifies against Meridian, burning his career publicly, while Jonah arrives mid-session with the tax records and Grandma's letters. Emotional beat: public truth as climax; the room turns.

chapters.title: Harvest Day
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The rezoning fails; Meridian withdraws. The community turns out to pick the crop together, and Theo, jobless, asks for nothing — just a place to stand beside her. Emotional beat: abundance earned through loss.

chapters.title: A New Menu
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She converts the café's back room into an orchard storefront — pies from Hollow Creek fruit — and offers Theo a partnership built on full disclosure this time. Emotional beat: rebuilding on honest foundations rather than rescue.

chapters.title: The Muscle Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Quiet domesticity: early mornings, flour on his sleeves, Jonah teaching him lamination. He admits he stopped trying to contain his heart somewhere around pruning season. Emotional beat: tenderness without defense.

chapters.title: First Fruit
chapters.summary: Shared closing POV. One year later, they host a harvest festival under the oldest tree, where Grandma's letters are read aloud. Jonah concedes the heart was never a muscle to train but a thing that ripens. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance understood as what we choose to keep growing.
